title: Meta Graph Learning for Long-tail Recommendation

problem.claim: Highly skewed item distributions hurt recommendation performance on tail items, particularly in graph-based recommendation models.

gap.claim: Auxiliary graph learning for long-tail recommendation must address downstream long-tail bias and possible negative transfer to the original user-item graph.

contributions.claim: A coupled framework learns item relations as an auxiliary graph to enhance graph-based representations for recommendation.
A meta-learning strategy tunes an edge generator to reconstruct a debiased item co-occurrence matrix and virtually evaluates generated item relations for recommendation.
A popularity-aware contrastive learning strategy aligns confident head-item representations with those of the learned auxiliary graph to prevent negative transfer.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe Meta Graph Learning as a novel and innovative framework for long-tail recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on public datasets reportedly show significant improvement over strong baselines for tail items without compromising overall performance.

narrative_sequence.summary: Long-tail item skew harms tail-item performance in recommendation systems.
Auxiliary graph learning faces long-tail bias and negative-transfer risks.
MGL uses meta-learning for debiased edge generation and popularity-aware contrastive learning.
Public-dataset experiments report better tail-item performance while preserving overall performance.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method targets tail-item gains while explicitly preserving overall recommendation performance.

interpretation.claim: Long-tail interventions may need safeguards against degrading performance on better-represented items.

application.claim: When designing long-tail recommendation methods, evaluate both tail-item performance and overall performance.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this trade-off is preserved across specific datasets, metrics, or deployment settings.

unknowns: Specific datasets, metrics, and quantitative gains are not provided.
The abstract does not report ablations, implementation details, or computational costs.
